7 - KEY WORKFLOWS (end to end, left -> right)
- Fix system SMTP login (535) -> test reset + notification email
- Reconnect Gmail with read permission; add Gmail addresses as test users in Google Cloud; live-test reply sync
- Try a real Google Sheet import + Sync now
- Public HTTPS URL (cloudflared tunnel) -> re-test opens/clicks
- AWS account -> file SES request first (2 weeks), Bedrock access (~$200)
- D-A product name + domain (blocks legal pages, DNS)
- Merge google-stack into main? (Gemini, reply sync, sender edit)
- Private DB/Redis networking, Redis TLS + password
- Smart segment with invalid tag id fails silently
- E2E gaps: add campaign step, add leads to segment, Sheets screens
- AI emails come back as one paragraph; a {first_name} without fallback seen once
T10.1 acceptance with a real send + reply -> T10.3 deliverability check (seed inboxes, spam score, DKIM alignment) ->
T10.4 production deploy -> T10.7 first beta users
T8.1 roll-ups, Outlook sender, Stripe billing, WhatsApp / SMS / LinkedIn, warm-up network, custom-domain white-label,
Elasticsearch, Datadog, fully automatic AI replies, A/B auto-winner.
Trade-off: one API process runs HTTP, websockets and every worker. Simple to run and deploy today; split workers into
their own service when send volume grows (JOBS_SCHEDULER=off on extra web instances).
Bottleneck: tracking, click and unsubscribe links point at API_URL. On localhost no open/click is ever recorded and
emails look spammy. Fix = public HTTPS URL (tunnel or hosting).
Trade-off: Postgres RLS isolates tenants even if a query forgets WHERE org_id. Cost: a SET per transaction and
SECURITY DEFINER functions for the few cross-tenant scans (scheduler, reply sync).
Scale: schedules live in Redis and Socket.io uses the Redis adapter, so the API can run as several instances behind a
load balancer (websocket transport only, no sticky sessions needed).
Why: AI behind one provider seam (AI_DRIVER mock | bedrock | gemini). Bedrock stays the main path; Gemini lives on
google-stack to test with real AI until AWS is ready. Mock keeps tests offline.
CAP: CP. Single Postgres primary, strong consistency for sends and suppression (never email someone who unsubscribed).
Redis holds only jobs + counters, so losing it delays work but loses no data.
